value.rationale: The source identifies first periodic-driver fold events as the mechanism for attractor–repeller collisions. Which of the fixed cat orbit and two inequivalent primitive-two cat orbits loses its fiber pair first is therefore a motivated dynamical question. The finding proves a sharp three-regime ordering with exactly two crossover phases and quantifies their phase sensitivity across an entire forcing interval. This is not a generic one-step stability check or symmetric-slice count; it converts previously plotted short-period bifurcation competition into a complete analytical classification within a stated natural parameter window. Higher periods and full collision threshold explicitly remain open.
